facts.statement: Magnosaurus means 'large lizard' and was a theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of England.
facts.quote: Magnosaurus (meaning 'large lizard') was a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of England.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest Magnosaurus could reach 4 meters in length, 1.5 meters in height, and weigh 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: llegó a medir 4 metros de largo 1,5 de alto y pesar 200 kilogramos

facts.statement: A 2010 estimation by Roger Benson suggested Magnosaurus weighed about half a tonne and stood over a metre at the hip.
facts.quote: Benson sin embargo, en 2010 dio una estimación más alta de aproximadamente media tonelada alcanzando el animal más de un metro en la cadera

facts.statement: The type material included partial dentaries, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, parts of the right pubis, internal casts of the femur, and tibiae, possibly from a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: El material incluía partes del dentario, vertebrás dorsales y caudales, partes del pubis derecho, cara interna del fémur y la tibia, de un posible individuo juvenil.

facts.statement: Until the 1990s, the genus Magnosaurus was generally ignored and treated as a species of Megalosaurus.
facts.quote: Hasta la década de 1990, el género había sido ignorado como una especie de Megalosaurus.

facts.statement: Magnosaurus is classified within the superfamily Megalosauroidea.
Magnosaurus belongs to the family Megalosauridae.
Magnosaurus is placed in the subfamily Afrovenatorinae.
Magnosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 175 to 170 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 175 y 170 millones de años, entre el Aaleniense y el Bajociense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Rauhut (2003) debated that Magnosaurus and Eustreptospondylus were the same genus, citing shared features like an expanded dentary tip and enlarged third dentary tooth.
facts.quote: Rauhut (2003) considered it and Eustreptospondylus to be the same genus, because the two share a similarly expanded front tip of the dentary and enlarged third dentary tooth.

facts.statement: Rauhut (2003) placed Magnosaurus with Eustreptospondylus due to similarities in the dentary and an elongated outer tooth.
facts.quote: Rauhut (2003) considera esto y lo coloca junto con Eustreptospondylus, debido a similitudes en el dentario y a ercer diente alargado

facts.statement: Revisions classify Magnosaurus as a basal tetanuran within Megalosauroidea, possibly a Megalosaurid and Eustreptospondylinae.
facts.quote: Revisiones lo colocan como un tetanuro basal, Megalosauroidea, posiblemente un Megalosauridae. Eustreptospondylinae.

facts.statement: In 2012, Carrano and colleagues placed Magnosaurus in the subfamily Afrovenatorinae.
facts.quote: En 2012 carrano et al. lo colocó en la subfamilia Afrovenatorinae.

facts.statement: Magnosaurus differs from Megalosaurus in that the latter has a distally compressed tibia.
facts.quote: por ejemplo en Megalosaurus la tibia está comprimida en distal, a diferencia de Magnosaurus

facts.statement: Magnosaurus lived during the Bajocian stage, between 170.9 and 168.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bajocian (170.9 to 168.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Magnosaurus is Eustreptospondylinae.
Magnosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: Magnosaurus was a bipedal carnivore of moderate size for a dinosaur.
rejected.quote: It would have been a bipedal carnivore of moderate size for a dinosaur.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a bipedal carnivore of moderate size for a'

rejected.statement: Friedrich von Huene named the species Megalosaurus nethercombensis in 1923 based on a partial skeleton found in the 19th century near Nethercomb, Dorset, England.
rejected.quote: In 1923, Friedrich von Huene named Megalosaurus nethercombensis from a partial skeleton (OUM J12143) from the Bajocian age Middle Jurassic Inferior Oolite, found in the nineteenth century by W. Parker near Nethercomb, north of Sherborne, in Dorset, England.

rejected.statement: Magnosaurus is considered the oldest certain known member of the Tetanurae, dating to about 175 million years ago.
rejected.quote: at about 175 million years old the oldest certain known member of the Tetanurae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the oldest certain known member of the Tetanurae'

rejected.statement: A 2010 redescription by Roger Benson concluded that Magnosaurus is a valid taxon and the oldest certain known member of the Tetanurae.
rejected.quote: A detailed redescription by Roger Benson in 2010 concluded Magnosaurus was valid taxon, a megalosaurid megalosauroid, and at about 175 million years old the oldest certain known member of the Tetanurae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the oldest certain known member of the Tetanurae'

rejected.quote: M. woodwardi was based on a tibia (BMNH R.3542) from the Lower Lias, which he simultaneously and accidentally also named Sarcosaurus andrewsi; in 1956 the latter name was given priority by von Huene.
